title: A third off the frame cost, a sun that sets behind its cloud, blue water, real meteor showers, and QF Textures v2
intro: Your round 8 answers are built in. Your main note was the cost: round 8's dearest frame was 4.6 ms on High against a 3 ms budget. The cost this round is mostly the light shafts and the dust that lives in them, so their march is rebuilt: fewer, jittered steps, the dust worked out inside the shaft march, and the dust skipped where no beam is. High frames now cost 3.3 ms at most (round 8: 4.6). That is still up to 0.3 ms over the 3 ms budget on the sea, swamp and river views, so High is close, not done; the views without much water cost 1.9 to 2.9 ms. Low at 1080p costs at most 0.86 ms (budget 0.9, round 8 1.32) and Potato at 720p at most 0.29 ms (budget 0.4). What changed in the look: Motes in the forest beam are still the weak spot: only one or two show in its upper part. The forest's leaves lose most of their cream veil (the beam dust no longer hangs over a ray that ends on leaves); the cream sky round the gap is still there. The golden-hour artifacts you saw in every texture photo are gone: the lit rectangle over the grass and the orange 'coins' were torchlight from the test house showing in daylight, and the radial streaks are much fainter. As a side effect, torchlight outdoors in the daytime is now about 70% weaker; at night it is unchanged. Low sun now lays a warm light on sunlit grass tops. The ocean's sun path is 12 to 20% brighter and longer. Clouds in front of the sun now hide its disk: at this sunset the sun sets behind its cloud bank. River beds are clearer, and the yellow stripes along the ledges are gone. Under water, rivers, lakes and the ocean are now blue-teal with blue sunbeams; swamps stay green. Meteor showers are rebuilt from how real ones look: one point in the sky per night, streaks that run away from it, short near it and long far from it, most faint and white, a few bright and tinted, now and then a fireball. Not changed this round: metal blocks (the cheap reflection that would not cost anything is next), the noon clouds' streaks (see the clouds question), vibrance. Four questions need your call: keep the fast volumetrics as the default, the weaker daytime torchlight, the sun behind its cloud, and whether the noon-cloud fix is worth a small cost. Costs are per frame on High at 1440p, against the same view with shaders off. After the shader questions come the textures: QF Textures v2 against v1 and Faithful 64x, and the potions. Credits: Faithful 32x and 64x (faithfulpack.net, Faithful License v4) in the v1, v2 and Faithful frames; the normal and specular maps are converted from Vanilla Normals Renewed by Poudingue (github.com/Poudingue/Vanilla-Normals-Renewed-1.12).

scenes.name: The cost, and the fast volumetrics
scenes.question: You said round 8 was over budget and must not kill anyone's game. The fast volumetrics (a new setting, on by default) cut the High frame by about 1.3 ms and Low by about 0.5 ms. They change the look a little: the shafts take 14 steps instead of 20, jittered so they do not band, and the dust is thinned where no beam is. A and B are the golden-hour plains with it on and off; C and D the forest beam, cropped, on and off. The ms under each is the measured cost.
scenes.notePrompt: Keep the fast volumetrics as the default? Can you see a difference?

options.critic: Critic 7: The tex-golden artifacts are gone at sheet scale: no lit rectangle over the grass, no orange coins; only a few pale flecks and flowers in the near field. The sunlit terrace tops read warm yellow-green, the shade stays cool green, the rose horizon band and warm far haze are kept. Fix: the faint diagonal streaks on the shaded field (not shafts).

options.label: Fast volumetrics off
options.critic: Critic 7: Fast volumetrics off: at sheet scale the same frame as A (a few more pale flecks in the near field), for 4.33 ms against A's 2.87. The fast path costs nothing visible here; keep it as the default.

options.label: Forest beam, fast on
options.critic: Critic 6: The beam haze lies over the path right of the big trunk and reads as a shaft; ground, trunks and leaves clean. Few separate motes. Fix: real motes inside the lit air.

options.label: Forest beam, fast off
options.critic: Critic 6: Fast off: the haze over the path is if anything weaker in this frame than A's, so the 14-step jittered march loses no beam; no banding in either. Supports QF_VOL_FAST 1 as the default.

scenes.name: The sun behind its cloud
scenes.question: You said clouds in front of the sun must dim it. The clouds round the setting sun were drawn faint at that distance and also stopped hiding the disk, so the disk showed whole through them. Now the cloud hides the disk: in this sunset the sun sets behind its cloud bank, a thin crescent shows under it and the glow round it stays. A is new, cropped round the sun at twice the size, B round 8.
scenes.notePrompt: Keep the sun behind the cloud, or is a hidden sun at this sunset a loss?

options.label: New
options.critic: Critic 7: The sun now sets behind its cloud bank: a thin white crescent under the cloud base where round 8 drew a whole disk through the cloud, with the warm aureole kept. The path on the water reads longer and brighter than p8's. A small green glint sits on the water left of the centre island at the horizon. Fix: the hidden disk takes away the frame's focal point; let thin cloud fringes show the disk's edge.

options.label: Round 8
options.critic: Critic 7: Loop 4 sunset. The disk has form (about 55 to 60 px across at 2560 wide, crisp and white) and a real warm aureole now: the sky above it falls from about 254,205,163 just off the rim to 181,145,118 some 350 px out, so the glow is there, not painted. Still weak: the glitter path under the sun measures 77 mean luma against r007 qw's 86 (uj was 66), so it is shorter and dimmer than r007 and far from BSL's column; the open water is dark navy at sunset; a few warm dust flakes float in front of the island, outside any beam. Fix: a longer, brighter sun path on the water.

scenes.name: Golden hour: artifacts gone, warm light on the grass
scenes.question: You found 'weird artifacting in all photos' of the golden plains. It was the shader, not the textures: the lit rectangle over the grass and the orange coins were torchlight from the test house showing in daylight, and dark streaks fanned over the ground. Torchlight is now damped in daylight, so the rectangle and the coins are gone and the streaks are much fainter (some faint diagonal ones remain on the shaded field). The low sun now lays a warm light on sunlit grass tops; shade stays cool green. A is new, B with the dust off, C round 8. The side effect: torches and lamps outdoors in the daytime light about 70% less than before; at night nothing changed.
scenes.notePrompt: Are the artifacts gone for you? Is weaker daytime torchlight fine?

The sunlit terrace tops read warm yellow-green, the shade stays cool green, the rose horizon band and warm far haze are kept. Fix: the faint diagonal streaks on the shaded field (not shafts).

options.label: Dust off
options.critic: Critic 7: Dust off: nearly the same as A; the far warm haze is aerial, not dust, so dust adds little to this view and takes nothing from it (no coins either way).

options.critic: Critic 7: The olive cast is gone. The near grass measures 43,47,15 (rows 1000 to 1300) against uk's olive 72,59,17 and r007's 42,50,29; BSL is about 45,48,25. The rose horizon band and the warm far haze are kept. What still falls short of the reference: the near field is flat green with little warm low-sun light on the grass tops, and scattered yellow flakes dot the grass (r007 has them too). Fix: warm grazing light on the lit side of the slope.

scenes.name: Forest light: the cream veil
scenes.question: You and the critic named the forest's cream wash. It had two parts. The veil over the leaves was the beam dust: a ray that ends on leaves looks at the canopy, not across a beam, so it now takes 40% of the dust; the leaves are cleaner and greener. The cream sky round the gap comes from the shafts and is still there; two tries at it did nothing visible. A is new, B the old dust on the leaves, C round 8.
scenes.notePrompt: Is the canopy better? How much does the cream sky still bother you?

scenes.name: Motes in the sunbeam (motion clip)
scenes.question: Round 8's beam had a haze but no motes. The far motes were tested against a beam count that the cheaper march made too noisy to keep; they now test the shade on both sides of the beam. Honest note: the critic finds only one or two warm motes in the upper shaft, against the cliff, and none in the lower half, even in motion; the beam's haze in this crop is also a little fainter than round 8's. Motes in the beam are still the open fault. A is a six-second clip, then the still; B the beam haze off (the few motes stay); C round 8's clip.

options.critic: Critic 5: Beam haze off: the shaft disappears, and a few warm mote dots stay on the cliff (QF_MOTES is still on), more visible than in A, so the haze partly hides them.

options.label: Round 8, clip
options.critic: Critic 5: The new dust_b view works: a lit shaft crosses the near air in front of the trunks, and the clip plays (90 frames). But a max-minus-median motion map of the burst, at 8x gain over the beam, shows only the shaft haze shimmering and no point-like mote trails anywhere inside it; one large flake sits on the birch at the right. So the beam now carries a visible dust haze, but separate drifting motes are not there. Fix: real motes, a few px each, drifting through the lit shaft.

scenes.question: You and the critic found faint stripes along the ledges and murky green water. The water over the bed is clearer and the bed keeps its own teal; the yellow stripes (grass tops seen through the water) are gone, though the critic still sees pale mint dashes along the ledge edges and finds mid-river water green and opaque. No sun glint: in this view the sun is overhead behind you. A is new, B round 8.

scenes.name: Noon clouds (motion clip)
scenes.question: The noon sky still has its streaks fanning from the top of the sky. We tested finer sampling: no change, so it is the cloud shape itself, a flat pattern stretched up through the whole cloud layer. The fix gives the clouds a shape that changes with height, at the cost of one more texture read per cloud sample; we have not measured it yet (likely a few tenths of a ms on High). A is a clip of the noon sky, unchanged since round 8; B is round 8's clip.

scenes.name: Meteor showers (motion clip)
scenes.question: You said round 8's shower was 'shit flying in every direction'. A real shower comes from one point in the sky, its radiant, a different place each night. Streaks start away from it and run away from it, short near it, long far from it; most are faint and white, about one in six bright and tinted with a short train, now and then a fireball. A is a clip of a shower night facing away from the radiant, so the streaks run the same way; B a pinned pair by a developer switch (only one of the two is in this frame); C the new-moon lake on a shower night; D round 8's clip.
